doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Prohibited AI practices
summary: Lists AI practices that are prohibited in the Union, including manipulative or deceptive techniques, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring and certain biometric uses. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 added further points that apply from 2 December 2026.
excerpt: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (a) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques …
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF obtained from the EU Publications Office (CELEX 32024R1689); eur-lex.europa.eu HTML was not retrievable from this environment.

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
summary: Defines when an AI system is high-risk: as a safety component of a product covered by Annex I harmonisation legislation requiring third-party conformity assessment, or when listed in Annex III. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 inserted paragraphs 1a to 1c clarifying what counts as a safety component.
excerpt: In addition to the high-risk AI systems referred to in paragraph 1, AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk.
note: Amended text of Art. 6(1a)-(1c) verified against Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (CELEX 32026R1744), OJ of 24.7.2026.

title: Risk management system
summary: Requires a documented risk management system for high-risk AI systems, run as a continuous iterative process across the whole lifecycle, covering identification, estimation and mitigation of risks to health, safety and fundamental rights.
excerpt: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689).

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Data and data governance
summary: High-risk AI systems trained with data must use training, validation and testing data sets meeting quality criteria on governance, representativeness and bias examination. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 replaced paragraphs 1 and 6 and deleted paragraph 5, cross-referring to the new Article 4a on bias detection.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria referred to in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of this Article and in Article 4a(1) whenever such data sets are used.
note: Excerpt is the text of paragraph 1 as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Technical documentation
summary: Technical documentation for a high-risk AI system must be drawn up before placing on the market, kept up to date, and contain at least the elements of Annex IV so that authorities can assess compliance.
excerpt: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up to date.
note: Second subparagraph of Art. 11(1) was replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

title: Record-keeping
summary: High-risk AI systems must technically allow automatic recording of events (logs) over the system lifetime, with logging capabilities that support traceability, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689); not amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
summary: High-risk AI systems must be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output and use the system appropriately, and must be accompanied by instructions for use with the information listed in this Article.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system's output and use it appropriately.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689).

title: Human oversight
summary: High-risk AI systems must be designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them while in use, with oversight measures proportionate to the risks, level of autonomy and context of use.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689).

title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
summary: High-risk AI systems must achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity and perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle, including resilience against attempts to alter their use, outputs or performance.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689).

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
summary: Deployers must take technical and organisational measures to use high-risk AI systems in line with the instructions for use, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data relevance, monitor operation and inform providers and authorities of risks and serious incidents.
excerpt: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use accompanying the systems.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689).

title: Deployer obligations — retention of automatically generated logs
summary: Deployers must keep the logs automatically generated by a high-risk AI system that are under their control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months, unless other Union or national law provides otherwise.
excerpt: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data.
note: Financial institutions may maintain these logs as part of documentation kept under Union financial services law (second subparagraph).

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
summary: People interacting directly with an AI system must be informed of that fact unless it is obvious; synthetic audio, image, video or text output must be marked in a machine-readable format; deployers must disclose emotion recognition, biometric categorisation and deep fakes.
excerpt: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed …
note: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 replaced Art. 50(7) (codes of practice) and gives providers of systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 until 2 December 2026 to comply with Art. 50(2). Status 2026-09-16: Article 50 has applied since 2 August 2026 and sits in the 3 % penalty band of Art. 99; the grace period for systems placed on the market before that date ends on 2 December 2026.

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems
summary: Providers must establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the technology and risks, systematically collecting and analysing performance data over the system's lifetime, based on a post-market monitoring plan that forms part of the Annex IV technical documentation.
excerpt: Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system.
note: Art. 72(3) was replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the Commission is to adopt guidance and a template for the plan by 2 September 2027.

title: High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)
summary: Lists the use-case areas whose AI systems are high-risk, including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, access to essential private and public services (including creditworthiness and insurance pricing), law enforcement, migration and administration of justice.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems pursuant to Article 6(2) are the AI systems listed in any of the following areas: 1. Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law … 2. Critical infrastructure …
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ PDF (CELEX 32024R1689).

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Entry into force and application
summary: Sets the staged application dates of the AI Act. As amended, Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025 (certain new prohibitions from 2 December 2026) and Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I high-risk systems.
excerpt: (c) Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I;
note: Excerpt is Art. 113, third paragraph, point (c) as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Consolidation note 2026-09-16: EUR-Lex still publishes no consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, so the amended dates were read from the amending Regulation itself. As amended: Annex III stand-alone high-risk systems 2 December 2027, Annex I high-risk 2 August 2028, the regulatory-sandbox deadline moved to 2 August 2027.

title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026 amends the AI Act to simplify implementation: it revises Articles 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 17, 25 to 30, 43, 50, 57 to 70, 72, 75 to 77, 111 and 113, inserts Article 4a on processing special categories of personal data for bias detection, and postpones the application of the high-risk rules.
excerpt: amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
note: Published in OJ L of 24 July 2026; enters into force on the third day following publication (27 July 2026). Verified via the EU Publications Office (CELEX 32026R1744).

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Processing of special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction
summary: Allows providers of high-risk AI systems, strictly for bias detection and correction under Article 10(2)(f) and (g), to process special categories of personal data where other data (including synthetic or anonymised data) would not suffice, subject to safeguards under EU data protection law.
excerpt: To the extent strictly necessary to ensure bias detection and correction in relation to high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 10(2), points (f) and (g), of this Regulation, providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons.
note: Inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1, point (6).

title: Scope — Union data protection law continues to apply
summary: Union law on personal data, privacy and confidentiality of communications applies to personal data processed under this Regulation; the GDPR and the ePrivacy rules are not affected.
excerpt: Union law on the protection of personal data, privacy and the confidentiality of communications applies to personal data processed in connection with the rights and obligations laid down in this Regulation. This Regulation shall not affect Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or (EU) 2018/1725, or Directive 2002/58/EC or (EU) 2016/680, without prejudice to Article 10(5) and Article 59 of this Regulation. 8.
note: Verified 2026-09-11 against the EUR-Lex HTML of the Official Journal text (CELEX 32024R1689); paragraph-level record added from the COMPL-AI (Guldimann et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.07959) technical interpretation, cited as the Act's own text.

title: Amending Annex III — corrigibility of outcomes as a criterion
summary: When the Commission assesses whether to add or modify a high-risk use case, one criterion is the extent to which the outcome produced with an AI system is easily corrigible or reversible; outcomes affecting health, safety or fundamental rights that cannot be corrected weigh towards high risk.
excerpt: the extent to which the outcome produced involving an AI system is easily corrigible or reversible, taking into account the technical solutions available to correct or reverse it, whereby outcomes having an adverse impact on health, safety or fundamental rights, shall not be considered to be easily corrigible or reversible;
note: Verified 2026-09-11 against the EUR-Lex HTML of the Official Journal text (CELEX 32024R1689); paragraph-level record added from the COMPL-AI (Guldimann et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.07959) technical interpretation, cited as the Act's own text.

title: Risk management system — required steps
summary: The risk management system is a continuous, iterative lifecycle process comprising identification of known and foreseeable risks, estimation and evaluation of risks under intended use and foreseeable misuse, evaluation of risks from post-market monitoring data, and adoption of targeted risk management measures.
excerpt: The risk management system shall be understood as a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system, requiring regular systematic review and updating. It shall comprise the following steps: (a) the identification and analysis of the known and the reasonably foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system can pose to health,

title: Data governance — examination for biases
summary: Training, validation and testing data sets must be examined for possible biases likely to affect health and safety, negatively impact fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, especially where outputs influence inputs for future operations.
excerpt: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where data outputs influence inputs for future operations; (g) appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f);

title: Data governance — relevance, representativeness and completeness
summary: Training, validation and testing data sets must be relevant, sufficiently representative and, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete for the intended purpose, with appropriate statistical properties for the persons or groups the system is intended to be used on.
excerpt: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose. They shall have the appropriate statistical properties, including, where applicable, as regards the persons or groups of persons in relation to whom the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.

title: Transparency — operation interpretable by deployers
summary: High-risk AI systems must be designed and developed so that their operation is sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately. An appropriate type and degree of transparency shall be ensured with a view to achieving compliance with the relevant obligations of the provider and deployer set out in Section 3. 2.

summary: The technical documentation must detail the monitoring, functioning and control of the system: its capabilities and limitations including accuracy for specific groups, foreseeable unintended outcomes and risk sources, the human oversight measures and interpretation aids, and input data specifications.

title: Technical documentation — description of the risk management system

title: GPAI technical documentation — training, testing and validation data
summary: GPAI model documentation must describe the data used for training, testing and validation, including type, provenance, curation, number of data points, scope and characteristics, how it was obtained and selected, and the measures to detect unsuitable sources and identifiable biases.

title: GPAI with systemic risk — evaluation strategies and results
summary: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must document their evaluation strategies and results, based on public evaluation protocols and tools or other methodologies, including evaluation criteria, metrics and the methodology for identifying limitations.

summary: Recalls the AI HLEG's seven non-binding principles — human agency and oversight; technical robustness and safety; privacy and data governance; transparency; diversity, non-discrimination and fairness; societal and environmental well-being; accountability — as guidance for coherent, human-centric AI without prejudice to the binding requirements.

title: Recital 75 — technical robustness and fail-safe behaviour
summary: Technical robustness is a key requirement for high-risk AI systems: they should be resilient to harmful or undesirable behaviour from limitations within the system or its environment, with measures such as fail-safe plans that safely interrupt operation on anomalies or outside predetermined boundaries.

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
summary: Before deploying an Annex III high-risk system, deployers that are public bodies or private entities providing public services, and deployers of the systems in Annex III points 5(b) and (c), must assess the impact on fundamental rights: the processes of use, the period and frequency of use, the categories of persons affected, the specific risks of harm, the human-oversight measures and the governance and complaint arrangements.
excerpt: (a) a description of the deployer's processes in which the high-risk AI system will be used in line with its intended purpose; … (e) a description of the implementation of human oversight measures, according to the instructions for use; (f) the measures to be taken in the case of the materialisation of those risks, including the arrangements for internal governance and complaint mechanisms.
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32024R1689). A drawing supplies the scaffolding — the deployment processes, the population reachable through the drawn path, the human-oversight step and the complaint or remediation component — and never the assessment's conclusion. Consolidation note 2026-09-16: EUR-Lex still publishes no consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, so the amended dates were read from the amending Regulation itself.

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Harmonised standards and standardisation deliverables
summary: High-risk AI systems and general-purpose AI models in conformity with harmonised standards whose references have been published in the Official Journal are presumed to meet the Chapter III Section 2 requirements to the extent the standards cover them.
excerpt: High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models which are in conformity with harmonised standards or parts thereof the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 shall be presumed to be in conformity with the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32024R1689). Status 2026-09-16: no reference has been cited in the Official Journal, so the presumption is not yet available to anyone and the requirements must be argued directly — EN 18286 was published in July 2026 but publication as a European Standard is not citation. Consolidation note 2026-09-16: EUR-Lex still publishes no consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, so the amended dates were read from the amending Regulation itself.

doc: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
title: Registration in the EU database
summary: Providers of Annex III high-risk systems register themselves and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market; a provider that has concluded under Art. 6(3) that its system is not high-risk registers itself and that system too; public-authority deployers register their use.
excerpt: Before placing on the market or putting into service an AI system for which the provider has concluded that it is not high-risk according to Article 6(3), that provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative shall register themselves and that system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32024R1689). Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 retained the registration of self-assessed non-high-risk systems in simplified form; check the amended wording against the consolidated text when EUR-Lex publishes it. Consolidation note 2026-09-16: EUR-Lex still publishes no consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, so the amended dates were read from the amending Regulation itself.
